question: Which papers jointly explain selected context frontiers and verifier-driven recovery?

candidate_papers.title: PaperServe: Context Frontiers for Evidence-Bounded Readers
candidate_papers.text: PaperServe defines the context frontier as the subset of evidence allowed into the reader, not the full retrieval set.

candidate_papers.title: Verifier Feedback for Paper Routing Recovery
candidate_papers.text: A verifier compares the drafted answer with selected evidence and asks retrieval to try again when required citations are absent.

candidate_papers.title: Vector Recall Is Not Context Routing
candidate_papers.text: Embedding search ranks related records but does not specify what the reader is permitted to see.

candidate_papers.title: Policy Gradient Tuning for Search Agents
candidate_papers.text: Policy-gradient training can tune action choices, but this benchmark is deterministic and does not train a policy.

expected_answer_points: The context frontier is the selected subset of retrieved evidence sent to the reader.
Verifier feedback can trigger another retrieval when selected evidence is incomplete.
Both gold papers are required for a complete synthesis.
